name: report_step3_output
description: Report step 3's final result: every candidate theoretical direction examined (examined_directions, including ones judged to 'not constitute a puzzle' and skipped), the two-tier structure of producing a research question — tier 1 is research_approach (gap_spotting or problematization, or empty if no direction constitutes a puzzle), tier 2 depends on tier 1 (under gap_spotting it's gap_type=theory_void/mechanism_gap, and mechanism_gap has a further tier 3, mechanism_gap_characterization=uncharted/anomalous_reversal; under problematization it's problematization_detail.assumption_type, per Alvesson & Sandberg 2011's methodology) — the research question itself, a coverage report, the rationale, and (if any) a cross-source tension note. Retrieval itself is done directly by step 3's agent calling the search_scopus tool exposed by atba/mcp_server.py; the retrieval strategy is in atba/prompts/retrieval_skill.md, and the gap-spotting/problematization judgment method is in atba/prompts/problematization_skill.md (both spliced into step 3's system prompt, see step3_system_prompt() in atba/prompts.py).

CitedEvidence.description:
The specific literature evidence a research-question statement cites — not a paraphrase, it must
be traceable back to a real retrieval result (echoing appendix B's "a research-question statement
must come with a traceable citation"). The Scopus API doesn't return full text, so citations can
only reach the abstract/metadata level — an inherent limitation of D.4's retrieval channel, not an
extraction oversight in this project.

authors.description: The author list — must not be left as a placeholder. The two sources differ in completeness; prefer the more complete one: under this key's entitlement, search_scopus only returns the first author. get_paper_abstract internally goes through Semantic Scholar/OpenAlex, which return a full author list along the way (this tool must be called before deciding to cite anyway to look up the abstract, and the author list comes back in the same call, no extra call needed). Approach: stash search_scopus's (first-author) value first, then replace it with the more complete version once get_paper_abstract returns non-empty authors; only fall back to search_scopus's first author if neither source finds any authors — never leave it blank. Even when get_paper_abstract doesn't find an abstract, its authors should still be used if non-empty — the abstract and the authors are two independent things.
authors.title: Authors

relevant_snippet.description: The specific excerpt or point from the abstract/metadata that supports the judgment — must not be just the paper's title
relevant_snippet.title: Relevant Snippet

abstract.description: The raw full abstract text obtained by calling the get_paper_abstract tool, copied verbatim, not rewritten/condensed — relevant_snippet is your own excerpt supporting the judgment, while abstract is the raw material a reviewer can use to independently verify whether relevant_snippet takes something out of context or over-interprets — the two must not be the same text, each serving its own purpose. If get_paper_abstract returns an empty abstract (Scopus itself doesn't have an abstract for this paper), honestly leave it blank, don't fabricate one.
abstract.title: Abstract

CitedEvidence.title: CitedEvidence

DirectionSearchRecord.description:
The complete exploration record for one of step 2's candidate theoretical directions — the
conclusion reached after attempting the retrieval_skill's three-tier degrading retrieval protocol.
Step 3's output must include every direction examined, not just report the one finally selected
(echoing the design where "trying the other directions step 2 matched" matters — the directions
that were skipped are themselves part of the audit requirement, proving they were genuinely tried
rather than fabricated).

queries_tried.description: Every search query actually used with search_scopus for this direction, in the order tried (including rewrite retries)
queries_tried.title: Queries Tried

verdict.description: The conclusion for this direction: e.g. 'the literature already fully explains the phenomenon, no puzzle here' / 'constitutes a theoretical void' / 'constitutes a mechanism gap, the gap is in...' / 'this direction's literature implies assumption X, in tension with the phenomenon, problematizable' / 'retrieval tool failure, cannot judge.' Rendered as Markdown by the frontend — when there are multiple reasons/points, separate them with a real blank line, don't write one unbroken paragraph; cite specific papers in standard APA author-year format (e.g. '(Zhao et al., 2017)'), not the informal 'journal abbreviation + year + topic tag' style (e.g. 'SMJ 2022 (multilevel OD)')
verdict.title: Verdict

DirectionSearchRecord.title: DirectionSearchRecord

GapType.description:
The **second tier** of producing a research question — used only when
research_approach=gap_spotting, corresponding to the two gap types originally defined in the
technical appendix's §A/§B. When research_approach=problematization, the corresponding tier-2 type
is ProblematizationDetail.assumption_type (see ProblematizedAssumptionType), not this enum — the
two paths' tier-2 type systems don't share the same field.
GapType.title: GapType

HitLevel.description:
The retrieval-hit tier — not free text; testing found that letting the model write this field
itself produces descriptive sentences like "retrieval could not be executed (a tool-environment
failure, not a hit-tier judgment)" instead of one of four fixed tiers, and the code can't reliably
distinguish "genuinely exhausted all three tiers with no hit" from "retrieval never really ran" —
two entirely different situations — from such prose. Two explicit infrastructure-failure values
were added to make this distinction structured, so there's no need to parse the agent's natural
language.
HitLevel.title: HitLevel

MechanismGapCharacterization.description:
The **third tier** of producing a research question — used only when gap_type=mechanism_gap
(theory_void has no such tier: there's no literature to speak of, so "would applying the logic
straightforwardly predict the opposite direction" is moot). Distinguishes two qualitatively
different kinds of "gap." Per Whetten (1989)'s "What Constitutes a Theoretical Contribution?" (AMR
14(4): 490-495): merely pointing out "existing theory doesn't cover this" is not by itself
sufficient grounds for a theoretical contribution (original: "discovering that a mainstream model
has low predictive validity ... does not by itself constitute a theoretical contribution. theorists
need to understand why this anomaly exists") — the truly weighty evidence is "applying existing
theory's core logic straightforwardly here would yield a prediction that contradicts/opposes the
phenomenon"; in that case step 4's task isn't simply "filling a gap" but "revising the theory," a
far stronger basis for contribution than mere non-coverage.

This distinction was proven necessary in testing: in run b45f39c3's phenomenon, ODT's prediction
for a same-cohort-peer reference frame (inverted-U) versus its prediction for a base-model reference
frame (if the same balancing logic is applied straightforwardly, also inverted-U) — what was
actually observed was the opposite, a U-shape. This isn't "ODT hasn't studied this" — it's "ODT's
core logic predicts the wrong direction here" — but the original mechanism_gap type conflated these
two cases, causing both step 4 and step 6 to treat it as merely "filling an unexplored gap,"
weakening the stronger theoretical significance this phenomenon actually carried.
MechanismGapCharacterization.title: MechanismGapCharacterization

ProblematizationDetail.description:
Required when research_approach=problematization, left blank otherwise. The structure
corresponds to the core output of Alvesson & Sandberg's (2011) methodological principles 2 through
6: identify the assumption → assess it → construct an alternative assumption → self-check against
Davis's (1971) obvious/absurd/interesting three-way test. Not a free-text paragraph — it's meant to
force the agent through these specific steps of judgment, rather than jumping straight to the
conclusion "I think there's an assumption worth challenging here.

identified_assumption.description: An assumption identified from the actually retrieved literature that this direction's literature widely shares but rarely states outright/questions — must be read out of real retrieval results, not guessed from common sense about what this field 'should' assume
identified_assumption.title: Identified Assumption

assumption_evidence.description: Specific citations (with abstracts) supporting 'this really is an assumption this body of literature shares' — cannot assert that an entire line of literature shares an assumption based on just one paper's wording
assumption_evidence.title: Assumption Evidence

why_worth_challenging.description: Why this assumption is worth challenging: whether it's widely shared yet weakly argued for on its own terms, whether it's starting to lose explanatory power, and — most importantly — which specific part of the phenomenon card is in direct tension with this assumption (cannot just abstractly say 'this assumption is imperfect')
why_worth_challenging.title: Why Worth Challenging

alternative_assumption.description: The alternative assumption direction proposed after the challenge — must be constructed from the literature actually read, not a wholesale adoption of a ready-made opposing paradigm (e.g. reflexively applying an entire poststructuralist/feminist framework) as the alternative assumption — the A&S original calls this 'prepackaged problematization,' not genuine problematizing
alternative_assumption.title: Alternative Assumption

interestingness_check.description: A self-assessment of alternative_assumption against Davis's (1971) three-way test: 'that's obvious' (too close to the audience's existing assumption, no point in challenging it) / 'it's absurd' (too total a denial, readers won't accept it) / 'that's interesting' (partly affirms, partly denies the existing assumption — the ideal zone) — only landing in the interesting zone lets this direction be adopted as the final research question; if the self-assessment lands on obvious or absurd, state so honestly and explain in rationale why it fell back to gap-spotting
interestingness_check.title: Interestingness Check

ProblematizationDetail.title: ProblematizationDetail

ProblematizedAssumptionType.description:
The five types of problematizable assumption Alvesson & Sandberg (2011) propose, ordered from
narrow to broad in scope/depth — the **tier-2** type for the research_approach=problematization
path (symmetric to GapType, the tier-2 type for the gap_spotting path), used only under that path,
to keep the agent from vaguely claiming "this assumption is problematic" without first
characterizing which type the assumption it identified is, then constructing an alternative
assumption using the method appropriate to that type (see problematization_skill.md).
ProblematizedAssumptionType.title: ProblematizedAssumptionType

ResearchApproach.description:
The **first tier** of producing a research question: gap-spotting or problematization —
corresponding to the top-level framework of Alvesson & Sandberg's (2011) "Generating Research
Questions Through Problematization" (AMR 36(2): 247-271) itself, which is the paper's actual
structure: two paths for constructing a research question are distinguished first, each with its
own specific types (tier 2) underneath.

**Changed this round from a "pick-one-of-three flat enum" to a "two-tier structure"**: an earlier
design crammed theory_void/mechanism_gap/problematization into the same flat
`ResearchQuestionType` enum, conflating "which path to take" (tier 1) with "which specific type
within that path" (tier 2) — that's not the paper's actual structure; the paper explicitly states
gap-spotting and problematization are "two starkly different ways of constructing a research
question," each with its own subtype system (theory_void/mechanism_gap under gap-spotting; the five
types of problematizable assumption A&S propose under problematization, see
ProblematizedAssumptionType) — not three options at the same level.

The two aren't mutually exclusive (the A&S original explicitly notes this): gap-spotting is
management's dominant approach (empirical statistics A&S cite show ~93% of published research is
gap-spotting), but tends to produce contributions that are "incremental but not very interesting";
problematization is rarer and has a higher bar, but is more likely to produce theory that's
"interesting" in Davis's (1971) sense, and hence more influential. By design, the agent isn't
required to pick one upfront — instead, while retrieving and reading literature for a candidate
direction, it applies both lenses at once (see problematization_skill.md), preferring
problematization unless it fails the check of "not too obvious, not too absurd," in which case it
falls back to gap-spotting — this is the A&S original's own position, not a shortcut this project
invented.
ResearchApproach.title: ResearchApproach

TheoreticalGroundingRecord.description:
A dedicated deep-retrieval pass on the anchor theoretical direction, building up that theory's
current state of research — **moved from step 4 to step 3 this round** (previously the output of
step 4's sub-step 0, see git history; a methodology discussion pointed out: "abduction is about
finding what ODT hasn't done; this step should retrieve ODT but from a different angle" — assigning
this to step 3, which already handles "the relationship to the anchor theory," so step 4 could
devote its retrieval budget entirely to "stepping outside the anchor theory to find a mechanism,"
see MechanismGroundingRecord).

Only run on **the one direction the research_question locked onto**, not on every direction in
examined_directions — step 3's earlier "broad and shallow" scan across candidate directions is
unchanged; only once a direction is confirmed to constitute a gap and a research_question is about
to be produced does it shift into this "narrow and deep" mode, completed right there in the same
agent run, not as a separate call.

Different in nature from step 3's earlier "broad and shallow" scan: that scan only needs to confirm
a direction constitutes a gap and then stops, without needing to fully map that direction's
literature; this is "narrow and deep" — having already decided to produce a research question on
this direction, it needs to work out whether there's any unresolved tension within that direction's
own literature (such tensions are often exactly where a candidate theory is most worth cutting in,
see the empirical case in run b45f39c3), serving as the "state of the anchor theory" background for
step 4's candidate generation (not the source of a mechanism a candidate theory borrows — that's
left to step 4's own MechanismGroundingRecord to find elsewhere).

anchor_theory.description: The name of the theoretical direction this deep retrieval anchors on, i.e. anchor_theory_direction
anchor_theory.title: Anchor Theory

queries_tried.description: Every search query actually used with search_scopus, in the order tried
queries_tried.title: Queries Tried

key_findings.description: Key literature retrieved that constitutes this theory's current state of research (including the raw abstract text obtained via get_paper_abstract) — when step 4 generates candidates, judgments like 'why the existing construct doesn't sufficiently cover the research question' must find corresponding support here; it can't fill in details missing here from a background impression of this theory drawn from training knowledge
key_findings.title: Key Findings

established_boundary_conditions.description: A summary of this theory's currently known boundary conditions/scope of applicability — reasoned from the literature in key_findings item by item, not a vague generalization. When mentioning a specific paper, use standard APA author-year format (e.g. '(Zhao et al., 2017)'), not the informal 'journal abbreviation + year + topic tag' style (e.g. 'SMJ 2022 (multilevel OD)') — this field gets integrated into the formal report by step 6, and informal citation formats would carry through into the final deliverable
established_boundary_conditions.title: Established Boundary Conditions

internal_tensions_or_gaps.description: Whether the literature in key_findings contains mutually contradictory findings, unresolved controversies, or a shared blind spot — such tensions are often exactly where a candidate theory is most worth cutting in; record them honestly, don't smooth them over just because they 'look messy.' Same as above, cite specific papers in standard APA author-year format, not journal-abbreviation-plus-topic-tag style
internal_tensions_or_gaps.title: Internal Tensions Or Gaps

TheoreticalGroundingRecord.title: TheoreticalGroundingRecord

input_schema.description:
The complete structured result step 3's single agent run requires the model to produce.

"Stopping once a direction produces a candidate research question, without examining the rest of
the candidate directions" is allowed by design (exhaustively testing every candidate direction is
not required), but examined_directions must honestly include every direction **actually examined**,
including ones judged to "not constitute a puzzle" and skipped — this is the baseline for
auditability; it cannot leave only the "finally selected" one and hide the exploration process.

examined_directions.description: Every candidate theoretical direction examined, in the order examined
examined_directions.title: Examined Directions

research_approach.description: The **tier-1** choice for producing a research question: gap_spotting or problematization. Empty if every direction was judged to 'not constitute a puzzle' (escalated to human review).

gap_type.description: **Tier 2** — required only when research_approach=gap_spotting: theory_void or mechanism_gap. Must be left blank when research_approach=problematization — that path's tier 2 is problematization_detail.assumption_type, not this field; the two paths' tier-2 type systems don't share this field.

research_question.description: The specific research question (RQ) produced; empty corresponds to the escalate-to-human branch
research_question.title: Research Question

anchor_theory_direction.description: The candidate theoretical direction the research_question anchors on when one is produced, which must exactly match one entry's theory_name in examined_directions (the direction that produced this research question). Required whenever research_question is non-empty — this information used to live only in the natural-language prose of verdict/rationale; step 4 needs a structured field to reliably locate 'which theory to run deep retrieval on,' rather than guessing by parsing prose.
anchor_theory_direction.title: Anchor Theory Direction

problematization_detail.description: The tier-2 choice and full methodological output for the research_approach=problematization path (including the five-way assumption_type classification) — required only when research_approach=problematization; must be left blank when research_approach=gap_spotting, not filled in perfunctorily just to have something there

mechanism_gap_characterization.description: **Tier 3** — required only when gap_type=mechanism_gap, left blank in every other case (theory_void or the problematization path). Distinguishes whether this gap is 'existing theory genuinely hasn't studied this' (uncharted) or 'applying existing theory's core logic straightforwardly here would yield a prediction that contradicts/opposes the phenomenon' (anomalous_reversal) — the latter is a far weightier basis for theoretical contribution than the former (Whetten 1989). Choosing anomalous_reversal requires spelling out in rationale exactly which of existing theory's core logic, what it would predict if applied straightforwardly, and which specific observation of the phenomenon it contradicts — not a vague 'feels like a conflict'; if that reasoning can't be laid out clearly, honestly choose uncharted instead of picking anomalous_reversal just because it 'sounds weightier.'

coverage_report.description: An overall summary of retrieval coverage: how many directions were searched and to what extent each was covered. Rendered as Markdown by the frontend — when describing multiple directions/points separately, separate entries with a real blank line, or write them as a Markdown ordered list (one item per line); don't write one unbroken paragraph, and don't write a literal backslash-n for a line break (that isn't a real line break, and the frontend will display it verbatim) — a reviewer needs to be able to spot where the points are at a glance. When mentioning a specific paper, use standard APA author-year format (e.g. '(Zhao et al., 2017)'), not the informal 'journal abbreviation + year + topic tag' style (e.g. 'SMJ 2022 (multilevel OD)') — this field gets integrated into the formal report by step 6
coverage_report.title: Coverage Report

rationale.description: Why the process finally settled on this direction/this research-question type (or why every direction was judged to not constitute a puzzle); if a tradeoff was made between problematization and gap-spotting, explain the basis for it. Same as above, separate multiple reasons with Markdown paragraphs/numbered lists rather than one unbroken paragraph; cite specific papers in standard APA author-year format too, not journal-abbreviation-plus-topic-tag style
rationale.title: Rationale

cross_source_tension_note.description: If there's tension/a contradictory finding between at least 2 sources in cited_evidence, flag it explicitly here — don't average it out or selectively ignore it to paper over the disagreement. When listing multiple tensions, use a Markdown paragraph/numbered list rather than one unbroken paragraph; cite specific papers in standard APA author-year format too, not journal-abbreviation-plus-topic-tag style
cross_source_tension_note.title: Cross Source Tension Note

anchor_theory_grounding.description: Required whenever research_question is non-empty: a dedicated deep-retrieval pass run on anchor_theory_direction (the sub-step moved over from step 4 this round, see TheoreticalGroundingRecord's module-level comment) — run only on this one locked-in direction, not on every direction in examined_directions. Left blank when research_question is empty (the escalate-to-human branch) — there's no point deep-diving a direction that didn't end up producing a research question.

input_schema.title: Step3Output
